主要内容: Dominion Energy, Inc. (NYSE: D) and SCANA Corporation (NYSE: SCG) announced an agreement for a stock-for-stock merger. SCANA shareholders will receive 0.6690 shares of Dominion Energy common stock for each share of SCANA common stock, valued at approximately $55.35 per SCANA share, representing a 30.6% premium. The merger is valued at approximately $14.6 billion, including debt assumption. The deal includes a $1.3 billion cash payment to SCE&G customers, a 5% rate reduction, and a $575 million refund. SCANA would operate as a subsidiary of Dominion Energy, maintaining its local presence and management structure. The merger is expected to be accretive to Dominion Energy's earnings in 2018 and increase its earnings-per-share growth rate to 8% or higher. The transaction aims to provide immediate savings for SCE&G customers and protect SCANA employees and shareholders. The merger is contingent upon shareholder approval, regulatory clearances from the U.S. Federal Trade Commission (FTC) and Department of Justice (DOJ), and authorizations from the Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) and Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC). The combined company will operate in 18 states, serving 6.5 million regulated customers with a 31,400 megawatt electric generating portfolio and 106,400 miles of natural gas pipelines. Customer refunds and rate reductions are expected to be effective within 90 days of the merger closing, subject to approval by the Public Service Commission of South Carolina. Dominion Energy and SCANA Corporation have announced an all-stock merger, with an immediate cash payment of $1,000 to the average South Carolina Electric & Gas residential electric customer. The merger is expected to combine Dominion Energy's extensive operations with SCANA's regional presence, enhancing their market position in the energy sector. Dominion Energy, one of the largest energy utility companies in the United States, serves nearly 5 million homes and businesses across 18 states. SCANA, based in Cayce, South Carolina, is an energy-based holding company with operations in electric and natural gas utility services. The merger is subject to regulatory approvals and shareholder consent, with potential risks including delays or abandonment due to regulatory hurdles or competing offers. The transaction will be submitted to SCANA's shareholders for consideration, with detailed information provided in the registration statement filed with the SEC. Shareholders will have access to free copies of the definitive proxy statement/prospectus and other relevant documents filed with the SEC. These documents will provide important information about the transaction and the companies involved. The merger is subject to regulatory approvals and other conditions. The transaction is expected to be completed in the near future, pending the necessary approvals.
